subject: math
title: Grade 8 Best Buys: Unit Prices, Discounts, Coupons, GST and PST
seo_title: Grade 8 Best Buys Worksheets: Unit Price, Discounts and GST + PST (Free Math, Answer Key, BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on best buys for the BC curriculum: unit prices, comparing sizes, discounts and coupons, 5% GST and 7% PST on purchases, and real best-buy decisions. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Compare unit prices, not totals: price ÷ amount, for the same unit.
key_sub: Take the discount or coupon off first, then add tax: 5% GST and 7% PST make 12% on most items in BC, so multiply by 1.12.
body_html:
Unit price: the price for one unit

A unit price is the price for 1 item, 1 kg, 1 L or 100 g. Divide the price by the amount: unit price = price ÷ amount. Always put the price first.

Example

A 3 kg bag of apples costs $5.97. What is the price per kilogram?

$5.97 ÷ 3 = $1.99.

Answer: $1.99 per kilogram

Compare sizes with the unit price

To find the best buy, compare the price for the same amount. Change the units first if you need to: 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 L = 1000 mL. The bigger package is often cheaper per unit, but not always.

Discounts and coupons

A percent discount is a percent of the regular price: 25% off means you pay 75%, so multiply by 0.75. A coupon for dollars off is subtracted. When there are two percent discounts, take the second one from the new price.

GST and PST in BC

Most things you buy in BC have 5% GST and 7% PST added, 12% in total, so the total is price × 1.12. Some items have only GST, such as children’s clothing, restaurant meals and printed books. Take the discount or coupon off first, then add the tax to the price you actually pay.

Best-buy decisions

A best buy is not only the lowest unit price. Think about how much you need, how much you will use before it spoils, shipping, fees and tax. Compare the total you will really pay for what you need.

Example

A pool charges $6.50 per swim or $55 for a 10-swim pass. You will swim 10 times. Which is cheaper?

Each swim: 10 × $6.50 = $65. Pass: $55. $65 − $55 = $10.

Answer: The pass, by $10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the totals of different sizesCompare unit prices, such as per 100 g or per litre
Dividing the amount by the price (3 ÷ $5.97)Divide the price by the amount: $5.97 ÷ 3
Comparing 400 g with 1 kg without changing unitsChange to the same unit first: 1 kg = 1000 g
25% off $60 = $60 − 25 = $35Find 25% of $60 ($15), then subtract: $45
Adding tax before taking off a $10 couponTake the coupon off first, then add 12% to what is left
Writing 20% off and 12% tax as “8% off”Multiply: price × 0.80 × 1.12
Adding PST to children’s clothing, restaurant meals or booksThese have 5% GST only

faq.q: How do you find the best buy in Grade 8 math?
faq.a: Find the unit price of each option by dividing the price by the amount, using the same unit for each, such as per 100 g or per litre. The lowest unit price is the best buy, as long as you need and will use that amount.

faq.q: How do you calculate the total with GST and PST in BC?
faq.a: Multiply the price by 1.12, because 5% GST plus 7% PST is 12%. For example, $80 × 1.12 = $89.60. Items with GST only, like children’s clothing, are multiplied by 1.05.

faq.q: Is the discount taken before or after tax?
faq.a: Stores take the discount or coupon off first and then add tax to the price you pay. For a percent discount the total is the same either way, but a dollar-off coupon taken before tax also saves the tax on that amount.

faq.q: What is financial literacy in the Grade 8 BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 8, the BC curriculum’s financial literacy standard is best buys: comparing unit prices, discounts, coupons and sales tax to make good spending choices. These worksheets give 100 practice questions with an answer key.

items.q: A 4-pack of yogurt cups costs $6.00. What is the price per cup?
items.e: Unit price = price ÷ number of items. $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50 per cup. ($24.00 multiplies; $0.67 divides the wrong way, 4 ÷ 6; $2.00 subtracts.)

items.q: A 2 L carton of milk costs $4.80. What is the price per litre?
items.e: $4.80 ÷ 2 = $2.40 per litre. ($9.60 multiplies; $0.42 is 2 ÷ 4.80, the wrong way round; $2.80 subtracts 2.)

items.q: A box of 12 granola bars costs $5.40. What is the price per bar?
A 3 kg bag of Okanagan apples costs $5.97. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: $5.97 ÷ 3 = $1.99 per kilogram. ($17.91 multiplies; $0.50 is 3 ÷ 5.97; $2.97 subtracts 3.)

items.q: A 500 g block of cheese costs $7.50. What is the price per 100 g?
items.e: 500 g is 5 groups of 100 g. $7.50 ÷ 5 = $1.50 per 100 g. ($15.00 is the price per kilogram; $0.15 divides by 50; $37.50 multiplies by 5.)

items.q: A 6-pack of sparkling water costs $4.50. What is the price per can?
A 400 g bag of trail mix costs $6.00. Which calculation gives the price per 100 g?
items.e: 400 g is 4 groups of 100 g, so share the price among 4: $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50. 4 ÷ $6.00 is upside down, and $6.00 ÷ 400 gives the price per gram.

items.q: A 1.5 kg bag of rice costs $4.50. What is the price per kilogram?
A 750 mL bottle of olive oil costs $9.00. What is the price per 100 mL?
items.e: 750 mL is 7.5 groups of 100 mL. $9.00 ÷ 7.5 = $1.20 per 100 mL. ($12.00 is the price per litre; $0.12 divides by 75; $6.75 multiplies by 0.75.)

items.q: A pack of 8 AA batteries costs $11.92. What is the price per battery?
items.e: $11.92 ÷ 8 = $1.49 per battery. ($95.36 multiplies; $0.67 is 8 ÷ 11.92; $3.92 subtracts 8.)

items.q: A 250 g box of BC blueberries costs $4.00. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, which is 4 boxes of 250 g. 4 × $4.00 = $16.00 per kilogram. ($1.60 is the price per 100 g; $62.50 is 250 ÷ 4; $0.16 divides by 25.)

items.q: A driver pays $70.00 for 40 L of gas. What is the price per litre?
A 2 kg bag of flour costs $5.20. What is the price per 100 g?
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g, which is 20 groups of 100 g. $5.20 ÷ 20 = $0.26 per 100 g. ($2.60 is the price per kilogram; $0.52 divides by 10; $0.13 divides by 40.)

items.q: A dozen eggs costs $5.88. What is the price per egg?
A 400 g fillet of wild BC salmon costs $11.60. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: 400 g = 0.4 kg. $11.60 ÷ 0.4 = $29.00 per kilogram. Check: 0.4 × $29 = $11.60. ($2.90 is the price per 100 g; $4.64 multiplies by 0.4; $46.40 multiplies by 4.)

items.q: A 400 mL bottle of shampoo costs $6.80. What is the price per 100 mL?
items.e: 400 mL is 4 groups of 100 mL. $6.80 ÷ 4 = $1.70 per 100 mL. ($0.59 is 4 ÷ 6.80; $27.20 multiplies; $1.36 divides by 5.)

items.q: A 3 L jug of apple juice costs $7.00. What is the price per litre, rounded to the nearest cent?
items.e: $7.00 ÷ 3 = 2.333…, which rounds to $2.33 per litre. ($0.43 is 3 ÷ 7; $21.00 multiplies; $2.34 rounds the wrong way: the next digit is 3, so round down.)

items.q: Cheese at the deli costs $2.35 per 100 g. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, which is 10 groups of 100 g. 10 × $2.35 = $23.50 per kilogram. ($235.00 multiplies by 100; $2.35 is still the price per 100 g; $0.24 divides by 10.)

items.q: Trail mix in the bulk bin costs $2.20 per 100 g. How much do 350 g cost?
items.e: 350 g is 3.5 groups of 100 g. 3.5 × $2.20 = $7.70. ($6.60 uses only 3 groups; $0.63 divides by 3.5; $22.00 is the price per kilogram.)

items.q: A pack of 3 toothbrushes costs $7.47. At the same unit price, how much would 5 toothbrushes cost?
items.e: Unit price: $7.47 ÷ 3 = $2.49. Five toothbrushes: 5 × $2.49 = $12.45. ($12.47 adds 5 to the price; $37.35 is 5 × $7.47, five whole packs; $14.94 is two packs.)

items.q: Which box of cereal is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Compare the price per 100 g, not the total price. Box A: $4.80 ÷ 4 = $1.20 per 100 g; Box B: $8.25 ÷ 7.5 = $1.10 per 100 g. Box B has the lowest price per 100 g, so it is the best buy. (Box A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which carton of orange juice is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per litre
items.e: Compare the price per litre, not the total price. Carton A: $2.60 ÷ 1 = $2.60 per litre; Carton B: $4.80 ÷ 2 = $2.40 per litre. Carton B has the lowest price per litre, so it is the best buy. (Carton A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which bottle of ketchup is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per 100 mL
items.e: Compare the price per 100 mL, not the total price. Bottle A: $2.25 ÷ 3.75 = $0.60 per 100 mL; Bottle B: $6.50 ÷ 10 = $0.65 per 100 mL. Bottle A has the lowest price per 100 mL, so it is the best buy. The biggest size is not always the best buy.

items.q: Which carton of eggs is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per egg
items.e: Compare the price per egg, not the total price. Carton A: $4.80 ÷ 12 = $0.40 per egg; Carton B: $6.84 ÷ 18 = $0.38 per egg. Carton B has the lowest price per egg, so it is the best buy. (Carton A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which bag of pasta is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Compare the price per 100 g, not the total price. Bag A: $1.75 ÷ 5 = $0.35 per 100 g; Bag B: $3.15 ÷ 9 = $0.35 per 100 g. The unit prices are equal, so neither is a better buy.

items.q: Which pack of paper towels is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per roll
items.e: Compare the price per roll, not the total price. Pack A: $8.40 ÷ 6 = $1.40 per roll; Pack B: $15.60 ÷ 12 = $1.30 per roll. Pack B has the lowest price per roll, so it is the best buy. (Pack A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which pack of AA batteries is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per battery
items.e: Compare the price per battery, not the total price. Pack A: $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25 per battery; Pack B: $13.00 ÷ 10 = $1.30 per battery. Pack A has the lowest price per battery, so it is the best buy. The biggest size is not always the best buy.

items.q: Which bag of rice is the best buy?
c: They all cost the same per kilogram
items.e: Compare the price per kilogram, not the total price. Bag A: $3.20 ÷ 1 = $3.20 per kilogram; Bag B: $6.00 ÷ 2 = $3.00 per kilogram; Bag C: $16.00 ÷ 5 = $3.20 per kilogram. Bag B has the lowest price per kilogram, so it is the best buy. (Bag A has the lowest total, but you get less.) The biggest size is not always the best buy.

items.q: Which bag of coffee is the better buy? (1 kg = 1000 g)
c: Both cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Compare the price per 100 g, not the total price. Bag A: $10.20 ÷ 3.4 = $3.00 per 100 g; Bag B: $27.00 ÷ 10 = $2.70 per 100 g. Bag B has the lowest price per 100 g, so it is the best buy. (Bag A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which bottle of sparkling juice is the better buy? (1 L = 1000 mL)
c: Both cost the same per 100 mL
items.e: Compare the price per 100 mL, not the total price. Bottle A: $3.00 ÷ 7.5 = $0.40 per 100 mL; Bottle B: $7.00 ÷ 20 = $0.35 per 100 mL. Bottle B has the lowest price per 100 mL, so it is the best buy. (Bottle A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which package of cheddar is the better buy? (1 kg = 1000 g)
c: Both cost the same per 100 g
items.e: Compare the price per 100 g, not the total price. Pack A: $6.30 ÷ 4.5 = $1.40 per 100 g; Pack B: $15.60 ÷ 12 = $1.30 per 100 g. Pack B has the lowest price per 100 g, so it is the best buy. (Pack A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which pack of sparkling water is the best buy?
c: They all cost the same per can
items.e: Compare the price per can, not the total price. Pack A: $4.20 ÷ 6 = $0.70 per can; Pack B: $7.80 ÷ 12 = $0.65 per can; Pack C: $16.80 ÷ 24 = $0.70 per can. Pack B has the lowest price per can, so it is the best buy. (Pack A has the lowest total, but you get less.) The biggest size is not always the best buy.

items.q: Which pack of soap bars is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per bar
items.e: Compare the price per bar, not the total price. Pack A: $4.50 ÷ 3 = $1.50 per bar; Pack B: $11.60 ÷ 8 = $1.45 per bar. Pack B has the lowest price per bar, so it is the best buy. (Pack A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which jug of laundry soap is the better buy?
c: Both cost the same per load
items.e: Compare the price per load, not the total price. Jug A: $9.60 ÷ 32 = $0.30 per load; Jug B: $17.92 ÷ 64 = $0.28 per load. Jug B has the lowest price per load, so it is the best buy. (Jug A has the lowest total, but you get less.)

items.q: Which bottle of olive oil is the best buy? (1 L = 1000 mL)
c: They all cost the same per 100 mL
items.e: Compare the price per 100 mL, not the total price. Bottle A: $6.50 ÷ 5 = $1.30 per 100 mL; Bottle B: $12.00 ÷ 10 = $1.20 per 100 mL; Bottle C: $37.50 ÷ 30 = $1.25 per 100 mL. Bottle B has the lowest price per 100 mL, so it is the best buy. (Bottle A has the lowest total, but you get less.) The biggest size is not always the best buy.

items.q: A 1 L carton of milk costs $2.10. A 4 L jug costs $6.00. How much do you save by buying the 4 L jug instead of four 1 L cartons?
items.e: Four cartons: 4 × $2.10 = $8.40. The jug: $6.00. Saving: $8.40 − $6.00 = $2.40. ($3.90 compares one carton with the jug, which are different amounts; $0.60 is the saving per litre; $8.40 is the cost of four cartons.)

items.q: A 2 kg bag of carrots costs $3.60. A 5 kg bag costs $8.50. How much less per kilogram is the 5 kg bag?
items.e: 2 kg bag: $3.60 ÷ 2 = $1.80 per kg. 5 kg bag: $8.50 ÷ 5 = $1.70 per kg. Difference: $0.10 (10¢) per kilogram. ($4.90 compares the totals; $1.70 is the unit price, not the difference; $0.50 is the saving on all 5 kg.)

items.q: Bakery A sells 6 muffins for $8.10. Bakery B sells 4 muffins for $5.60. How much would 12 muffins cost at the bakery with the lower unit price?
items.e: Bakery A: $8.10 ÷ 6 = $1.35 per muffin. Bakery B: $5.60 ÷ 4 = $1.40 per muffin. Bakery A is cheaper: 12 muffins = 2 boxes of 6 = $16.20. ($16.80 uses Bakery B; $11.20 is only 8 muffins; $13.70 adds the two prices.)

items.q: A 1.5 kg bag of apples costs $4.35. A 4 kg box costs $11.20. Which is the better buy, and by how much per kilogram?
c: The 1.5 kg bag, by $6.85 per kg
The 1.5 kg bag, by 10¢ per kg
The 4 kg box, by 10¢ per kg
They cost the same per kg
items.e: Bag: $4.35 ÷ 1.5 = $2.90 per kg. Box: $11.20 ÷ 4 = $2.80 per kg. The 4 kg box is cheaper by 10¢ per kilogram. ($6.85 is the difference between the totals, which are for different amounts.)

items.q: Which statement about best buys is true?
c: The package with the lower price is always the better buy
The bigger package is always the better buy
You cannot compare packages of different sizes
Compare prices for the same amount, such as per 100 g
items.e: A best buy has the lowest price for the same amount (the unit price). A bigger package is often cheaper per unit, but not always, and a lower total often means you just get less.

items.q: How much is the discount on this $60 rain jacket?
items.e: 25% of $60 = $60 ÷ 4 = $15. ($35 subtracts 25 dollars; $45 is the sale price, not the discount; $2.40 is 60 ÷ 25.)

items.q: A $48 pair of runners is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount: 25% of $48 = $12. Sale price: $48 − $12 = $36. ($23 subtracts 25 dollars; $12 is the discount; $60 adds 25%.)

items.q: What is the sale price of this pair of hiking boots?
items.e: You pay 70%: $90 × 0.70 = $63. Or: 30% of $90 = $27 and $90 − $27 = $63. ($60 subtracts 30 dollars; $27 is the discount; $117 adds 30%.)

items.q: This coupon is used on a $32 phone case. What is the price after the coupon?
items.e: $5 off means subtract 5 dollars: $32 − $5 = $27. ($30.40 treats it as 5% off; $37 adds; $1.60 is 5% of $32.)

items.q: Which calculation gives the sale price when an item is 35% off?
items.e: 35% off means you pay 100% − 35% = 65%, so price × 0.65. price × 0.35 gives only the discount.

items.q: A $75 backpack is 40% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: You pay 60%: $75 × 0.60 = $45. ($35 subtracts 40 dollars; $30 is the discount; $105 adds 40%.)

items.q: A $200 bike is 15% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $200 is $20 and 5% is $10, so 15% is $30. Sale price: $200 − $30 = $170. ($185 subtracts 15 dollars; $30 is the discount; $230 adds 15%.)

items.q: A $80 hoodie is on sale for $60. What percent is the discount?
items.e: Discount: $80 − $60 = $20. Compare it with the regular price: $20 ÷ $80 = 0.25 = 25%. (20% uses the dollars as the percent; about 33% divides by the sale price, $20 ÷ $60; 75% is the part you pay.)

items.q: This coupon is used on a $40 item. What percent of the price does it save?
items.e: $8 ÷ $40 = 0.2 = 20%. (8% uses the dollars; 5% is 40 ÷ 8; 80% is the part you still pay.)

items.q: A $45 game can be bought with 20% off or with a $10-off coupon. Which deal gives the lower price?
items.e: 20% off: 20% of $45 = $9, so $36. $10 off: $35. $10 off is better by $1. (20% off by $10 compares the numbers 20 and 10, not dollars.)

items.q: A $120 pair of skates can be bought with 15% off or with a $20-off coupon. Which deal gives the lower price?
items.e: 15% off: 15% of $120 = $18, so $102. $20 off: $100. $20 off is better by $2. (15% off by $5 compares 20 with 15, not dollars.)

items.q: A $78 order can use this coupon or a 20%-off coupon, but not both. Which coupon saves more?
items.e: 20% of $78 = $15.60 off. The $15 coupon takes $15 off. 20% off saves 60¢ more. (By $5 compares the numbers 20 and 15, not dollars.)

items.q: A store has a deal: buy one T-shirt, get the second one 50% off. Two $26 T-shirts are bought. What is the total before tax?
items.e: First: $26. Second: 50% off $26 = $13. Total: $26 + $13 = $39. ($26 treats the second as free; $52 forgets the deal; $13 is only the second shirt.)

items.q: Granola bars are $4.50 a box with a deal: buy 2, get 1 free. What is the price per box when you take 3 boxes?
items.e: You pay for 2 boxes: 2 × $4.50 = $9.00 for 3 boxes. Per box: $9.00 ÷ 3 = $3.00. ($1.50 is the price ÷ 3; $4.50 is the regular price; $2.25 is the price ÷ 2.)

items.q: A $45 hoodie is on clearance for 60% off. What is the clearance price?
items.e: You pay 40%: $45 × 0.40 = $18. ($27 is the discount; $44.40 subtracts 60¢; $72 adds 60%.)

items.q: A $150 snowboard is 20% off. At the till, the store takes another 10% off the sale price. What is the final price?
items.e: 20% off: $150 − $30 = $120. Another 10% off $120: $120 − $12 = $108. ($105 adds the percents to 30%, but the second 10% is taken from $120; $120 forgets the second discount; $42 is the total discount.)

items.q: An $80 jacket is 20% off. Then a $10-off coupon is used on the sale price. What is the final price before tax?
items.e: 20% off: $80 − $16 = $64. Coupon: $64 − $10 = $54. ($56 uses the coupon first and then takes 20% off $70; $50 takes 30 dollars off; $70 forgets the 20% off.)

items.q: A pair of ski goggles is 15% off. The sale price is $51. What was the regular price?
items.e: The sale price is 85% of the regular price. Regular price = $51 ÷ 0.85 = $60. Check: 15% of $60 is $9 and $60 − $9 = $51. ($58.65 adds 15% of $51 instead; $66 adds $15; $43.35 takes 15% off again.)

items.q: Simran has $50. A $64 hoodie is 25% off, and she uses a $5-off coupon on the sale price. How much money does she have left (before tax)?
items.e: Sale price: 25% of $64 is $16, so $48. Coupon: $48 − $5 = $43. Left: $50 − $43 = $7. ($2 forgets the coupon; $16 subtracts 25 dollars instead of 25%; $5.75 uses the coupon before the 25% off.)

items.q: Is 20% off and then another 10% off the same as 30% off?
c: No, it is 2% off in total
No, it is 32% off in total
No, it is 28% off in total
items.e: On $100: 20% off gives $80, then 10% of $80 is $8, so the price is $72. That is $28 off $100: 28% off in total. The second discount is taken from a smaller price.

items.q: A $60 lamp has 5% GST added. How much is the GST?
A $60 lamp has 7% PST added. How much is the PST?
items.e: 7% = 0.07. $60 × 0.07 = $4.20. ($7 uses the percent as dollars; $0.42 is 0.7%; $42 multiplies by 0.7.)

items.q: An $80 pair of headphones has 5% GST and 7% PST added. How much tax is that in total?
items.e: GST: $80 × 0.05 = $4.00. PST: $80 × 0.07 = $5.60. Total tax: $9.60 (12% of $80). ($12 adds 12 dollars instead of 12%; $4 is only the GST; $5.60 is only the PST.)

items.q: An $80 pair of headphones has 12% tax added (5% GST + 7% PST). What is the total price?
Which calculation gives the total price of an item with 5% GST and 7% PST added?
items.e: The total is 100% of the price plus 12% tax = 112% = 1.12. So price × 1.12. price × 0.12 gives only the tax.

items.q: A child’s snowsuit costs $40. Children’s clothing in BC has 5% GST but no PST. What is the total price?
items.e: Only GST applies: $40 × 0.05 = $2. Total: $40 + $2 = $42. ($44.80 adds 12%, but there is no PST; $47 adds $7; $2 is only the tax.)

items.q: A family’s restaurant meal costs $36 before tax. Restaurant meals in BC have 5% GST but no PST. What is the total?
items.e: GST: $36 × 0.05 = $1.80. Total: $36 + $1.80 = $37.80. ($40.32 adds 12%, but restaurant meals have no PST; $41 adds $5.)

items.q: A $22 novel is bought in Victoria. Printed books in BC have 5% GST but no PST. What is the total price?
What is the total on this receipt?
items.e: Add the subtotal and both taxes: $55.00 + $2.75 + $3.85 = $61.60. ($57.75 forgets the PST; $67 adds $12; $55.12 adds 12¢.)

items.q: A phone stand costs $14.99. How much is the 7% PST, rounded to the nearest cent?
items.e: $14.99 × 0.07 = $1.0493, which rounds to $1.05. ($1.04 cuts off the digits instead of rounding; $10.49 multiplies by 0.7; $1.80 is 12%, both taxes.)

items.q: The $14.99 phone stand has 5% GST and 7% PST added. What is the total price?
A $23 board game has 5% GST and 7% PST added. Noah pays with cash. How much does he pay?
items.e: Tax: $23 × 0.12 = $2.76. Total: $25.76. Canada has no pennies, so a cash total rounds to the nearest 5¢: $25.76 → $25.75. ($25.76 is what a card pays; $25.80 rounds up instead of to the nearest 5¢; $35 adds $12.)

items.q: A $90 adult rain jacket is 20% off. Then 5% GST and 7% PST are added. What is the total?
items.e: Sale price: $90 − $18 = $72. Tax: 12% of $72 = $8.64. Total: $72 + $8.64 = $80.64. ($82.80 combines 20% off and 12% tax into 8% off; $72 forgets the tax; $100.80 forgets the discount.)

items.q: A store takes 20% off an item and also adds 12% tax (GST + PST). Does the total change if the tax is added before the discount?
c: Yes, the total is 8% off either way
Yes, taking the discount first is cheaper
Yes, adding the tax first is cheaper
No, both orders give the same total
items.e: Both are multiplications: price × 0.80 × 1.12 = price × 1.12 × 0.80 = price × 0.896. The order does not matter for a percent discount. It is never “8% off”: that adds and subtracts the percents.

items.q: This coupon is used on a $45 sweater. 5% GST and 7% PST are added to the price after the coupon. What is the total?
items.e: Coupon first: $45 − $10 = $35. Tax: 12% of $35 = $4.20. Total: $35 + $4.20 = $39.20. ($40.40 adds the tax before taking off the $10: $50.40 − $10; $35 forgets the tax; $50.40 forgets the coupon.)

items.q: A $10-off coupon is used on an item with 12% tax (GST + PST). Which way gives the lower total?
c: Both ways give the same total
items.e: Before tax, the $10 is not taxed, so you also save 12% of $10 = $1.20 in tax. Taking the coupon off before tax is cheaper by $1.20. (Unlike a percent discount, a dollar coupon changes the total.)

items.q: A total of $44.80 includes 5% GST and 7% PST. What was the price before tax?
items.e: The total is 112% of the price, so price = $44.80 ÷ 1.12 = $40. Check: $40 × 1.12 = $44.80. ($39.42 takes 12% off the total, but the tax was 12% of the price; $32.80 subtracts $12; $50.18 adds tax again.)

items.q: Children’s running shoes cost $50 (5% GST only). Adult socks cost $15 (5% GST and 7% PST). What is the total for both?
items.e: Shoes: $50 + $2.50 GST = $52.50. Socks: $15 + $1.80 = $16.80. Total: $52.50 + $16.80 = $69.30. ($72.80 adds 12% to both; $68.25 adds only GST to both; $65 forgets the tax.)

items.q: A $35 water bottle is 20% off, then 5% GST and 7% PST are added. Leah pays with cash. How much does she pay?
items.e: Sale price: $35 − $7 = $28. Tax: 12% of $28 = $3.36. Total: $31.36. Cash rounds to the nearest 5¢: $31.35. ($31.36 is the card total; $31.40 rounds up; $39.20 forgets the discount.)

items.q: Kai has $60 in his bank account. He buys an adult hoodie for $45 and a cap for $8. Both have 5% GST and 7% PST. He pays by debit. How much is left?
items.e: Before tax: $45 + $8 = $53. Tax: 12% of $53 = $6.36. Total: $59.36. Left: $60.00 − $59.36 = $0.64. Debit is exact, so there is no rounding. ($7 forgets the tax; $0.65 rounds as if paying cash; $1.60 forgets the tax on the cap.)

items.q: The community pool in Nanaimo charges $6.50 per swim, or $55 for a 10-swim pass. Hana plans to swim 10 times. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
items.e: Paying each swim: 10 × $6.50 = $65. The pass: $55. $65 − $55 = $10, so the pass is cheaper by $10. ($48.50 is $55 − $6.50, which compares the pass with one swim.)

items.q: A ski hill near Kamloops sells day tickets for $95, or a 4-day pass for $340. How much does the pass save per day?
items.e: Pass per day: $340 ÷ 4 = $85. Saving per day: $95 − $85 = $10. ($40 is the saving for all 4 days; $85 is the pass price per day; $245 is $340 − $95.)

items.q: A climbing gym in Burnaby charges $18 per visit or $65 for a month. Zara climbs several times a month. What is the smallest number of visits in a month that makes the monthly pass cheaper?
items.e: $65 ÷ $18 ≈ 3.6. Three visits cost 3 × $18 = $54, less than $65. Four visits cost $72, more than $65. So the pass is cheaper from 4 visits. (3 rounds down; 47 is $65 − $18; 83 is $65 + $18.)

items.q: Blueberries cost $4.50 for a 500 g box, or $14.00 for a 2 kg flat. Ryan’s family will eat only 1 kg before the berries spoil. Which choice costs less for them?
items.e: They need 1 kg = two 500 g boxes: 2 × $4.50 = $9.00. The flat costs $14.00. Two boxes cost $5 less. The flat has the lower unit price (70¢ vs 90¢ per 100 g), but it is not a best buy if half of it is wasted.

items.q: Store A sells a jacket for $80 at 25% off. Store B sells the same jacket for $70 at 10% off. Both add 5% GST and 7% PST. Which store has the lower total?
items.e: Store A: $80 − $20 = $60, and $60 × 1.12 = $67.20. Store B: $70 − $7 = $63, and $63 × 1.12 = $70.56. Store A is lower by $3.36. ($3.00 is the difference before tax; Store B by $10 compares the regular prices.)

items.q: Hockey tape costs $3.29 a roll, or $8.97 for a 3-pack. A team needs 6 rolls. What is the lowest cost?
items.e: 3-pack: $8.97 ÷ 3 = $2.99 a roll, cheaper than $3.29. Six rolls = two 3-packs: 2 × $8.97 = $17.94. ($19.74 buys 6 single rolls; $26.91 buys 3 packs, which is 9 rolls; $8.97 is only 3 rolls.)

items.q: Jasleen can buy a speaker online for $54 plus $8 shipping, or at a store in Surrey for $59. Both prices include tax. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
items.e: Online: $54 + $8 = $62. Store: $59. The store is cheaper by $3. (Online by $5 forgets the shipping.)

items.q: Granola in the bulk bin costs $1.40 per 100 g. A 750 g bag of the same granola costs $9.75. How much do you save by buying the bag instead of 750 g from the bin?
A car uses 8 L of gas per 100 km. Gas costs $1.80 per litre. How much does the gas cost for a 160 km drive?
items.e: 160 km is 1.6 groups of 100 km, so the car uses 1.6 × 8 L = 12.8 L. Cost: 12.8 × $1.80 = $23.04. ($14.40 is 8 L for only 100 km; $230.40 puts the decimal point in the wrong place; $12.80 is the litres, not the cost.)

items.q: Gas costs $1.89 per litre at one station and $1.83 per litre at another. Olivia’s parent fills a 45 L tank. How much is saved at the cheaper station?
items.e: Saving per litre: $1.89 − $1.83 = $0.06. For 45 L: 45 × $0.06 = $2.70. ($0.06 is only one litre; $27.00 puts the decimal point in the wrong place; $6 reads 6¢ as $6.)

items.q: Juice boxes are $3.49 each, or 3 for $10. How much do you save by buying 3 at the deal price?
items.e: Three at $3.49: 3 × $3.49 = $10.47. Deal: $10.00. Saving: $0.47 (47¢). ($0.16 is the saving on one item, rounded; $6.51 is $10 − $3.49; $3.49 is one item.)

items.q: A warehouse store membership costs $65 a year and saves 8% on groceries. A family spends $900 a year there. How much does the family save in a year after paying for the membership?
items.e: Saving: 8% of $900 = $72. After the membership: $72 − $65 = $7. ($72 forgets the membership cost; $137 adds the fee; $65 is only the fee.)

items.q: A class needs 30 juice boxes for a field trip. Packs of 8 cost $5.60 and packs of 12 cost $8.88. What is the lowest cost to get at least 30 boxes?
items.e: Unit prices: $5.60 ÷ 8 = 70¢ and $8.88 ÷ 12 = 74¢, so packs of 8 are cheaper. Four packs of 8 give 32 boxes: 4 × $5.60 = $22.40. Two 12-packs and one 8-pack cost $23.36. ($21 is 30 × 70¢, but you cannot buy part of a pack; $26.64 is three 12-packs; $16.80 is only 24 boxes.)

items.q: Store A sells a pair of headphones for $75 plus 12% tax (GST + PST). Store B sells the same pair for $82 with tax included. Which is cheaper?
items.e: Store A: $75 × 1.12 = $84. Store B: $82. Store B is cheaper by $2. (Store A by $7 forgets to add the tax to Store A’s price.)

items.q: A bike costs $480 to buy, or $15 a day to rent. For how many days of renting does the rent add up to the price of the bike?
items.e: $480 ÷ $15 = 32 days. Check: 32 × $15 = $480. Renting for fewer days is cheaper; for more days, buying is. (465 is $480 − $15; 3.2 and 320 put the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: A school orders 30 T-shirts for its Terry Fox Run. Supplier A charges $12 a shirt. Supplier B charges $9 a shirt plus a $75 set-up fee. Which supplier is cheaper, and by how much?
items.e: Supplier A: 30 × $12 = $360. Supplier B: 30 × $9 + $75 = $270 + $75 = $345. Supplier B is cheaper by $15. (By $90 forgets the set-up fee; $72 compares $12 with $9 + $75 for one shirt.)

items.q: Ava and 5 teammates order 4 pizzas for take-out at $18.50 each. Prepared food in BC has 5% GST but no PST. They split the total equally. How much does each person pay?
items.e: Pizzas: 4 × $18.50 = $74.00. GST: $74 × 0.05 = $3.70. Total: $77.70. Six people: $77.70 ÷ 6 = $12.95. ($12.33 forgets the GST; $13.81 adds PST too; $19.43 splits among only 4 people.)

items.q: Liam wants a $320 bike. 5% GST and 7% PST are added. He has $110 saved and saves $30 a week. How many more weeks until he can buy it?
items.e: Total: $320 × 1.12 = $358.40. Still needed: $358.40 − $110 = $248.40. $248.40 ÷ $30 = 8.28, so round up to 9 weeks. (8 weeks rounds down and is $8.40 short; 7 weeks forgets the tax; 12 weeks forgets the $110 saved.)

items.q: Owen buys 3 adult T-shirts at $16 each. The deal is buy 2, get the third one 50% off. Then 5% GST and 7% PST are added. What is the total?
items.e: Before tax: $16 + $16 + $8 = $40. Tax: 12% of $40 = $4.80. Total: $44.80. ($53.76 forgets the deal; $40 forgets the tax; $35.84 treats the third shirt as free.)

items.q: A 1 kg tub of yogurt costs $6.00. A 500 g tub costs $3.75, and Mateo has a 50¢-off coupon for the 500 g tub. Which is the better buy for him?
c: They cost the same per 100 g
items.e: 1 kg tub: $6.00 ÷ 10 = 60¢ per 100 g. 500 g tub with the coupon: $3.75 − $0.50 = $3.25, and $3.25 ÷ 5 = 65¢ per 100 g. The 1 kg tub is still the better buy. (75¢ forgets the coupon.)
